name: Repair Clark County
area: Events around Clark County, run by Columbia Springs
notes: Volunteers fix small appliances, electronics, clothing, bikes, and more for free. Bring up to two items you can carry, and fix them alongside the volunteer.
notice: They can't take microwaves, gas-powered items, or anything hazardous.

name: Bike Clark County Community Bike Shop
notes: Full-service bike repair and used bikes. The shop supports youth bike-safety and mechanic programs.

name: Bob's Sporting Goods Bike Shop
notes: Full-service bike repair shop inside Bob's Sporting Goods.

name: Express Sewing
address: 10411 NE Fourth Plain Blvd #136, Vancouver, WA 98662
notes: Hems, patches, buttons, and garment repairs. Appointments only — leave a message or email.

name: Express Alterations
address: 8700 NE Vancouver Mall Dr, Ste 141, Vancouver, WA 98662
notes: Hems, taking in or letting out, and other alterations.

name: Prairie Electric
address: 6000 NE 88th St, Ste B104, Vancouver, WA 98665
notes: Residential service calls, including outlets, switches, panels, and older wiring.

name: Vancouver Washington Tool Library
notes: A nonprofit building a community tool library with repair classes.
notice: Not lending tools yet. Check their website for opening news.

name: Verify a contractor (WA L&I)
notes: Before you hire an electrician, plumber, or contractor, check that their Washington license, bond, and insurance are active.

name: Product recall search (CPSC)
notes: Search by brand or product. Recalled items are often repaired, replaced, or refunded for free.

name: Battery & hazardous waste drop-off (Clark County)
notes: Free disposal for Clark County residents. Never put batteries in the trash or curbside recycling — they can start fires in garbage trucks and recycling centers.
